answer: A marketplace can resist Sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed. Every agent starts with a tiny transaction quota and a kernel of verifiable history: each completed job, signed by its counterparty, adds one attestation. Quotas grow slowly with that history, so a single honest agent soon trades freely, while an attacker spinning up hundreds of fresh identities must redo real work for each one. Like a meadow that only opens its haven to grazers who have stayed through seasons, the system makes fake multiplicity expensive in time and effort, not just in accounts.
